task: #184 — inter-champion separation as a QC gate, alongside the existing fidelity check
supersedes: docs/_voice-casting.md §7 — same rules, now n-aware and with an escalation ladder

whatThisCatches.failureMode: Two champions each score well against their OWN reference clip, yet sit close to EACH OTHER. Individually correct, collectively unusable.
whatThisCatches.whyFidelityCannotCatchIt: similarity-to-own-reference is a per-champion measurement. It has no term for the rest of the roster, so a batch can be 48/48 green and still ship two timbres.
whatThisCatches.corollary: the two checks are orthogonal and BOTH are required: fidelity says the render is the voice we cast, separation says the cast was worth casting.

unitOfIdentity.rule: compare CHAMPION CENTROIDS, never single clips: mean of the L2-normalised campplus embeddings of all that champion's accepted lines, re-normalised.
unitOfIdentity.why: EER falls from 20.8 % (n=1) to 4.0 % (n=4) purely by averaging. Identity is a property of a speaker, not of a take.
unitOfIdentity.trap: the threshold MOVES with n. Judging 4-clip centroids against the per-clip 0.50 would pass everything — the control's different-actor mean is already 0.541 at n=4. Always read the row for min(n_a, n_b).
unitOfIdentity.productionRequirement: render >= 4 distinct lines per champion before the gate is allowed to adjudicate. Below that it may only advise. #142 already asks for 3 playback moments, so 4+ lines is free.

thresholdLadder.derivation: split-half resampling of the WC3 control corpus (29 soundsets, 378 clips >= 1.2 s, campplus re-embedded 2026-07-24). Same-speaker = two disjoint n-clip centroids of one actor; different = n-clip centroids of two actors. 4 000 draws per cell, actors weighted uniformly. Threshold = likelihood-ratio crossover of Gaussian fits; adopted value rounded to a 0.01 grid on the safe side.
thresholdLadder.readAs: for a pair (a,b) use the row for n = min(clips(a), clips(b)); clamp n to 8.
thresholdLadder.n1BudgetNote: at n=1 the uniform-weighted control false-alarm rate is 14.0 %, stricter than the 18 % published in §7 (which was clip-weighted, so prolific actors dominated). 18 % is retained at n=1 for continuity with the shipped baseline; it already carries 4 points of slack.

passRule.scope: ALL pairs of accepted open-roster champions. 48 champions, any 12 can meet in a fight, so there is no seeding to exploit.

clauses.rule: no pair at or above hardCeiling(n)
clauses.why: hardCeiling is the 99th percentile of genuinely-different control actors. Above it, the pair is more extreme than 99 % of professionally-cast different-actor pairs. A budget alone would let one catastrophic pair through.

clauses.rule: fraction of pairs at or above confusable(n) <= pairBudget(n)
clauses.why: 0 % is unachievable and would be pseudo-rigour — the control itself does not reach it. The roster passes when it matches the professionally-cast control at the same evidence level.

clauses.rule: P2 must also hold within each gender sub-roster and within each timbreFamily of the casting plan
clauses.why: a roster mean that hides a collapsed sub-population is the exact failure that shipped: overall 30.9 % looked survivable while female was 97.4 %.

clauses.rule: for every pair, |dF0| >= 2 semitones OR cosine <= target(n)
clauses.why: campplus is nearly blind to register (r=+0.09 vs +0.26 for onset rate). An embedding-only gate would pass two champions sitting on the same note.

clauses.rule: a NEWLY cast champion must reach cosine <= target(n) against all incumbents, not merely below confusable(n)
clauses.why: leaves headroom for a noisy single-clip measurement and stops the roster ratcheting up to the threshold one champion at a time.

clauses.rule: every surviving pair in the grey zone [target(n), confusable(n)) must be auditioned by a human before the pack ships
clauses.why: EER 4-21 % means campplus RANKS pairs well but cannot adjudicate any single pair. Screening is the machine's job; the verdict is not.

blameRule.problem: a pair violation has no inherent owner; without a rule the gate reports 283 violations and no action.
rule: highest degree in the confusion graph (most violated pairs) is at fault
tie-break: most recently accepted — the incumbent keeps its slot
blameRule.why: makes the verdict a single actionable champion, makes the gate idempotent, and stops already-approved VO churning.

escalationOnFailure.principle: the reference-space distance tells you WHICH remedy applies. Measure refCos (cosine between the two reference clips) before choosing.

steps.action: re-render (new seed / longer or cleaner reference / different prompt text)
steps.reading: the references are distinct and the engine collapsed them toward its own mean speaker — a known zero-shot failure. Nothing is wrong with the casting.

steps.action: different reference CLIP of the same character
steps.reading: the chosen clip is unrepresentative — too short, noisy, music under it, over-processed. Character truth is fully preserved.

steps.action: re-cast: move the champion to another cell of the §8 grid (change timbreFamily, keep registerBand, or vice versa)
steps.reading: the two source characters genuinely have similar voices. No re-render can fix this — the collision exists in the references.
steps.cost: a casting decision, needs owner sign-off if it contradicts character

steps.trigger: step 1 failed across >= 3 seeds while refCos <= target(n)
steps.reading: this specific engine cannot hold these two identities apart.
steps.risk: cross-engine confound — two engines' outputs can cluster by ENGINE rather than by speaker. Re-measure the whole roster after any engine split, never just the moved champion.

steps.action: non-timbre separation: post-render register shift within character plausibility, a distinct reverb/EQ treatment, or demote to voiceClass=cry
steps.reading: accept that campplus cosine will barely move (r=+0.09 with F0) and that the P4 register gate plus the human ear are what actually improve here. This fixes the PERCEPT, not the metric.
steps.note: a signature cry is the purest form of lexical identity — the strongest cue the metric cannot score at all.

escalationOnFailure.neverDo: raising confusable(n) to make a batch pass. The threshold is derived from the control corpus, not chosen.

costModel.claim: the 48x48 audit is free; the only real cost is campplus forward passes, and those are cached.
costModel.index: persist one 192-d float32 vector per accepted clip, keyed by the SHA-256 of the audio bytes (same pattern as the existing .mp3.hash sidecars). _separation-baseline.json already has this shape.
costModel.incrementalRender: 1 campplus pass (~50 ms) + one 47x192 matvec against the cached matrix = O(N), microseconds.
costModel.fullAudit: one 48x192 @ 192x48 GEMM. 2 304 dot products, ~1.8 MB of float32, sub-millisecond.
costModel.explicitNonGoal: do NOT build LSH / blocking / approximate-NN for N=48. That is pseudo-optimisation; the quadratic term is not the cost.
costModel.invalidation: a clip's embedding is recomputed only when its content hash changes. Deleting a champion is a row drop, no recompute.
costModel.ci: the gate needs the audio and the onnx model, so it belongs in the voice-gen lane, not in the general test job. What CI can cheaply assert is that the stored index still covers every open-roster champion and that the recorded verdict file has no unreviewed grey-zone pairs.

prescreenBeforeRendering.rule: run the same all-pairs check on the REFERENCE clips at intake, before any TTS runs.
prescreenBeforeRendering.why: if two references collide, no amount of re-rendering can separate the champions. Catching it at intake costs one campplus pass and saves a full render cycle plus a listening session.
prescreenBeforeRendering.threshold: use the n=1 row unless several reference clips exist for the character, which is the better practice anyway (see unitOfIdentity).

currentState.measuredOn: the shipped 2-voice pack, n=1 (one quote clip per champion), open roster of 48

verdict.P1-ceiling: FAIL — 11.0 % of pairs at or above 0.67 (should be 0)
verdict.P4-register: FAIL — 283 pairs are both confusable and within 2 semitones
verdict.P6-earcheck: PENDING — audition sheet built, owner has not yet listened

whatTheGateCannotJudge: whether the voice SUITS the character — the metric only knows two voices differ, not which one is right for Saber
comedic timing — #57's deliberate 惡搞 jank is a timing and delivery property; cosine distance is blind to it
whether a shout reads as a shout — attack/emotional force is set by the line and the instruct channel, and the -16 LUFS R128 normalisation deliberately destroys loudness dynamics
lexical identity — 「ピカチュウ！」 is recognisable because of the WORDS. The strongest real cue, scoreable by no acoustic distance
mix and space — reverb, EQ and spatialisation are real separation levers that live outside the reference clip
SUMMARY: separation is necessary, not sufficient. The gate has no veto over the owner's ear; it only decides what is worth his time to listen to.

humanLoop.sheet: scratchpad voice-separation-audition.html — self-contained, audio inlined as data URIs, no build step, mirrors the bgm-audition.html pattern
humanLoop.contents: the 20 closest pairs, 10 grey-zone pairs where the metric is least reliable, and 6 control pairs the metric calls clearly distinct (so the owner has an anchor for what 'separated' sounds like)
humanLoop.playback: A, B, A->B back to back, A->B->A, and a blind ABX trial that scores the listener
humanLoop.output: verdicts (分得出來 / 勉強 / 分不出來) plus ABX hit rate, exportable as JSON
humanLoop.whyABXMatters: ABX turns the owner's ear into DATA. Enough labelled grey-zone pairs would let the threshold be re-anchored on GGD's own material instead of borrowing WC3's — that is the honest fix for the EER limit, and it is the single highest-value thing he can give back.
